states.changed: A visitor meets every AI incident on record as a square in the order the database admitted it, lights them by whom the record names as harmed (people, people named by a product, the public, a good with no person in it, a firm), by who wrote first and by what was answered, reads any square's harmed parties, and watches goods named as harmed thicken from 11 of the first 198 entries to 143 of the latest full 200.

A visitor now meets thirty first reports as squares sorted by whether the harmed's own words are in them (15, 7 only through another, 8 not at all) and opens a note on each; lights the field by who the Field found wrote, by whom a public body's act lands on, and by the 219 entries that name one party as harmed and as deployer or developer; and reads which 44 of 150 names the sorting rule got wrong.

A visitor now meets a box saying what the check held and what it corrected: a named person's own words stand in 8 of the thirty first reports, not 15, with four bodies and ten told by others shown as their own groups; public acts are the Field's checked 60, 36 on the person who used the AI; the field crosses two questions and opens any incident by number or by stepping through the lit ones, thirty to a row on a phone; the drift chart splits epistemic integrity from privacy; and the page says who submitted the entries that name goods.

A visitor now meets the classed record as eight rows cut into six kinds of incident, with the part of each kind that names a good lit, and reads it three ways by a switch: as the record has it, with the kinds of incident held still (6 to 57 in 100) and with the naming held still (13 to 34, then flat); pressing a part follows its kind down the rows and shows scams going from 15 of 80 entries naming a good to 65 of 88.
